next_flight.countdown_target_note: SpaceX has not published a Flight 16 window. Wikipedia, citing a CADENA operations planning conference on 8 Oct 2026, lists NET 10 Dec 2026 from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A with a Starlink 30-1 payload. That date and site are unconfirmed by SpaceX.
next_flight.launch_site: Kennedy Space Center LC-39A (expected — unconfirmed by SpaceX)
next_flight.mission_notes: No official SpaceX launch date, vehicle assignment, or payload has been published for Flight 16. Public secondary sources point to a first Starship launch from LC-39A, NET 10 Dec 2026.

upcoming_flight_16.schedule_note: No official SpaceX launch date. Wikipedia, citing a CADENA operations planning conference, lists NET 10 Dec 2026 from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A for Starlink 30-1. That remains unconfirmed.

last_flight.catch_note: Ship catch time is T+22:32:34 on the SpaceX Flight 15 timeline, applied to the Wikipedia liftoff time of 22:47:36 UTC on 13 Nov 2026 (15 Nov 2026, 8:20 am AEDT / 14 Nov 3:20 pm CST / 4:20 pm EST). The official SpaceX catch post was published at 21:21:41 UTC.
last_flight.phase_note: Ship 42 was caught at the Pad 2 tower. Booster 22 aborted its catch and diverted offshore. Payload: all 26 Starlink V3 satellites deployed.
last_flight.mission_notes: First catch of a Starship upper stage (Ship 42) by the Mechazilla arms. Super Heavy booster 22 aborted the tower catch after an early boostback shutdown (low fuel mass; root cause under investigation), diverted to an offshore landing, hovered over the Gulf, and the flight termination system was triggered at landing-burn shutdown.
